_comment: A0-random of docs/2026-09-07_anytime_prediction_and_calibrated_eta_design.zh.md §2.2: the arm that reads the re-anchoring curve WITHOUT the distribution-shift cost. Every existing checkpoint was trained at the L-1 anchor only, so A0-fixed's later bins are out-of-distribution (the closure arm's 12 km vectored ADE went 2197 -> 6706 m in the review's replay). random_train_anchor=True trains at one uniformly random valid anchor per flight and epoch (min 20 s of future — NOT the 60 s the design doc first wrote: under a 60 s contract 3 of the 6851 train flights have no admissible anchor at all (their truth after L-1 is under 60 s; the fixed-anchor policy admits any positive future) and train() refuses to drop them silently; 20 s keeps the training cohort identical to every fixed-anchor arm — the pairing the arm exists for — and it is the regime the anytime curve most needs, the last seconds before the runway where the duration head floors. The replay's --min-future-s 60 is a different quantity: which BINS are readable, not which anchors are trained). The imitation teachers are anchor-bound (the inverse-dynamics one is a recorded performance cliff under random anchors, the fitted table is fitted at L-1), so the only screened supervision compatible with random anchors is L1.b's teacherless combination: heading-rate 8 + bank TV 1 (60-epoch screen: bank skill 0.711 vs the teacher control's 0.709, ADE not worse). Same base as l1b_full_arms.json, 180 epochs. READING (design doc §2.4): replay this checkpoint with run_ts_anytime_curve.py on the same remaining-path grid as A0-fixed, paired per flight and stratum with L1_native32 (fixed) — the difference at each bin is the distribution-shift cost, the shape of the A0-random curve is the anytime deliverable. VETO: A0-random at the L-1 bin worse than L1_native32 beyond seed noise (random-anchor training damaged the base). Known limit stated in advance: the duration head's ~125 s floor means |dt| p80 cannot fall under 30 s near the runway for ANY arm here; s_freeze is read where it can be, and the floor is the B-line's problem (quantile head). RESULT of the first arm (2026-09-07 night): the L-1 veto FAILED severely — ADE 2949 vs native32's 1322, FDE p50 3784 vs 864, win rate 6.8 % — but the run early-stopped at epoch 30 with its best at epoch 10 (every fixed-anchor arm trains 96-180 epochs) and its state/velocity components at that epoch were twice the fixed arms', i.e. an UNDERTRAINED model frozen by the selection rule: fixed-anchor-common-grid-ade scores the L-1 anchor only while training draws anchors uniformly, so once the model specialises across the anchor range the L-1 score stalls and patience 20 fires. The second arm is the cheap clean test: identical, patience 180 (early stopping off; selection still picks the best L-1 epoch). If its L-1 score keeps improving with budget, the first result was the stopping rule; if the best epoch stays early while the anytime curve improves, the selection METRIC is wrong for this arm and an anchor-grid validation metric (mean ADE over the remaining-path bins) is the next lever — that is code, pre-registered here, not improvised.

arms._comment: A1 (design doc §2.4, built 2026-09-07): the same arm as A0_random_hr8_tv1_p180, selected on `anchor-grid-common-grid-ade` instead of `fixed-anchor-common-grid-ade`. WHY, measured on the first arm: on the re-anchoring grid A0_random draws BETTER geometry than the fixed arm at EVERY anchor (chamfer p50 -114 to -524 m) and better ADE at <= 8 km, while the L-1 metric that selected its checkpoint scored 2949 m against native32's 1322 and early-stopped it at epoch 30 with its best at epoch 10. `fixed-anchor-common-grid-ade` scores the validation set at the L-1 anchor ONLY — the one anchor a random-anchor model is least specialised for — so it freezes such a model early on a metric blind to what the model improves. The new metric averages the SAME common-grid ADE over five anchor sets (L-1 and the 16/12/8/6 km remaining-path bins of `anchor_grid`, each flight at its own closest admissible sample), equal weight per set. The 20/4/2 km bins of the measurement grid are NOT selected on: 20 km covers ~35 % of the cohort and 4/2 km are partial-to-empty under the 60 s future floor. The 20/4/2 km bins of the measurement grid are NOT candidates: 20 km covers 33.7 % of the KRDU val cohort and 4/2 km are partial-to-empty under the 60 s future floor. Of the four candidates, a bin whose coverage falls under 50 % is DROPPED at plan build with a printed notice and a `dropped_bins` record — on THIS cohort that is 16 km (37 %; the median flight has 13.4 km left at L-1), so this arm is expected to be selected on L-1 + 12/8/6 km (78.7 % / 99.7 % / 99.7 %). Which bins survive is a property of the split, not of the model, so it is the same for every arm trained on it. READING, against the two earlier arms: (1) the best epoch — the p20 arm's was 10 and the p180 arm's is the control for 'was it only the stopping rule'; this arm's best epoch is the answer to 'was it the metric'; (2) the per-epoch `validation_anchor_grid` block in history.json — each anchor set's ADE and its flight count, so the curve's shape is visible during training instead of only in an A0 replay; (3) the L-1 veto is still READ (the block records `fixed_anchor_common_grid_ade_m` every epoch, the same number the other two arms selected on) but it is NO LONGER the selection: an arm whose L-1 score is worse than native32 beyond seed noise while its grid mean and its 16/12/8/6 km ADEs beat both earlier arms is the anytime deliverable, not a failure. Cost: ~5x the checkpoint-selection pass (four extra deployable replays of the validation split; the L-1 pass is reused, not rebuilt), measured at 0.046 -> 0.238 s per epoch on a synthetic control run. NOTE on comparing: the two earlier arms carry NO `validation_anchor_grid` block (they were trained before the metric existed), so their curves must come from an A0 replay of their checkpoints — `run_ts_anytime_curve.py` on the same grid. Compare mean-to-mean (this block's `mean_ade_m` against the mean of the replay's per-bin ADE MEANS): A0's own verdicts read the ADE p50, the package's convention for a heavy-tailed error, and a median is not the number this metric selects on. No numbers here yet — this arm has not been trained.
